title: Recipe 05 — Stateful Graph (three nodes, two edges, one human gate)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 05 is the shape when what runs next depends on what came before — conditional edges, durable checkpoints, a human in the loop.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The smallest spec — plan, execute, summarise

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape, pick the entry
beats.cue: “Four lines: the name, the graph spine, the model — and which node the run starts at.”

beats.label: Node 1 · plan
beats.cue: “Read the user's input from upstream state and produce a 3-bullet plan. Return only the plan, no preamble.”

beats.label: Node 2 · execute
beats.cue: “Read the plan from upstream state's plan field.” Each node's terminal text becomes the value under its own name — that is the whole state model.

beats.label: Put a human in the loop
beats.cue: “Two lines buy an approval gate: the runtime writes a checkpoint, prints hitl_pause, and exits cleanly. It never sits on a TTY waiting.”

beats.label: Node 3 · summarise, then wire the DAG
beats.cue: “A 2-sentence executive summary.” And the edges — nodes are inert until you connect them: plan → execute → summarise.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Graph well-formedness passes the compile path skips — dangling edges, unreachable nodes — plus a scope audit. Nothing emitted.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Three nodes, two edges, and the hitl prompt on execute — lowered to JSON. The edges carry from/to only: no when: predicate, so they're unconditional.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target graph (3 nodes, 2 edges, hitlPrompt on execute)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (3 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted graph
beats.cue: “addNode, addEdge, setEntry over a checkpoint store — and inside execute, a requestApproval call. The graph engine is a library, not a service.”

beats.label: Try to ship it to the edge
beats.cue: “Refused, and it says why: the human gate needs a host. The compiler won't drop the pause to make the spec fit a Worker.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1 — `cf-worker-graph does not support HITL in M2 (node "execute" has hitlPrompt); use the local graph target for HITL`

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A graph is compile-only — the CLI names the shapes it takes and exits 1.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1 — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "graph")`

beats.label: Boot the graph on a real question
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The graph reads its input from stdin — that seeds the plan node. Plan prints, execute prints, then the run stops at the gate and prints its own resume line.”
beats.command: echo "Should we adopt a 4-day work week?" | bun live/dist/agent.ts

verify.note: the recipe's own input; needs Anthropic credentials. Deps were installed by the --check beat. The pause exits the process cleanly — it does not hold a TTY

groups.title: One more thing · The pause is a checkpoint

beats.label: Find the gate in the emitted code
beats.cue: “The recipe's HITL contract, as code you can read: a checkpoint store, and requestApproval with the prompt from the spec verbatim.”

verify.note: the bundle imports createCheckpointStore, calls ctx.requestApproval("Approve the plan and continue to execute?"), and branches on a rejection helper — the pause is generated code, not runtime magic

beats.label: Look at the run on disk
beats.cue: [needs-key] “One directory per graph run, checkpoints inside it — state you can resume from or branch off.”

verify.note: the grun_… dir only exists after the keyed run above; CREWHAUS_CHECKPOINT_DIR moves the store elsewhere

beats.label: Approve, and let it finish
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Resume reads the checkpoint, injects the decision, and continues to summarise. The decision string is opaque — the node's instructions decide what it means.”

verify.note: resumes the newest graphRunId with decision `approve`; needs Anthropic credentials. Resume always lands on the most recent durable checkpoint, never partway through a node
